subegit: subigō, -ere, -ēgī, -āctum — to subdue, force, compel (3rd sg. perf.)
succedere: succēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to go under, come beneath (+ dat.) (pres. inf.)
suis: suus, -a, -um — his/her/its/their own (m./f./n. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.) · sūs, suis — pig (dat./abl. pl., rare)
suprema: suprēmus, -a, -um — highest, last, extreme (superl. of superus; f. nom./abl. sg.; n. pl.)
suum: sūs, suis (m./f.) — pig, boar, swine (gen. pl., = suum; not suus); also suus, -a, -um, his/her own (m. acc./n. nom./acc. sg.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (ex tantā urbe)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tecti: tectum, -ī (n.) — roof, house (gen. sg.) · also tectus, -a, -um — sheltered, covered; tegō perf. pass. part. (m. nom. pl.: tectī silvīs)
tempestas: tempestās, tempestātis (f.) — storm, weather, season (nom. sg.)
tenentem: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, grasp, keep (pres. part., m. acc. sg.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totum: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tyranni: tyrannus, -ī (m.) — ruler, despot, tyrant (gen. sg.) · also m. nom. pl. (tyrannī, the rulers)
tyrrhenum: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan; the Tyrrhenian sea west of Italy (n./m. acc. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
urguet: urgeō (urgueō), urgēre, ursī — to press, drive hard, push (3rd sg. pres.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
uterque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (m. nom. sg.)
vasta: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (f. abl. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
vecti: vehō, -ere, vexī, vectum — to carry; pass. to be borne, sail (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
veniens: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come, approach (pres. part., m./f./n. nom. sg.)
veri: vērus, -a, -um — true; vērum (n.), the truth (n. gen. sg., as noun)
vestra: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vestras: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (f. acc. pl.)
vestris: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
veteris: vetus, veteris — old, aged (m./n. gen. sg.)
veterisque: vetus, veteris — old, former, ancient (gen. sg.) + -que 'and'
vexit: vehō, -ere, vēxī, vectum — to carry, convey, bear along (3rd sg. perf.)
viae: via, -ae (f.) — road, way, journey (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
vinclo: vinc(u)lum, -ī (n.) — chain, bond, fetter (abl./dat. sg., shortened form of vinculo)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
vocari: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon, name (pres. pass. inf.)
vocatis: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (perf. pass. part., m./f./n. abl. pl.) · also m. dat. pl. (patribus … vocātīs)
voltus: vultus (voltus), -ūs (m.) — face, look, expression (nom. sg.; acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (haerent … voltus)
voluit: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want (3rd sg. perf.)
volvens: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, unroll, ponder (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
